endorsements.quote: Context-aware AI could in principle reduce bias by using individual baselines rather than population norms, but this benefit will only be realized if the underlying data and algorithms are developed with diverse training sets and equity-focused evaluation.

unlisted_practices: Conduct prospective studies demonstrating that context-aware monitoring leads to earlier intervention, reduced morbidity, and net clinical benefit across diverse populations before adopting it.
Conduct dedicated longitudinal evaluation of the psychological effects of iterative surveillance in healthy populations.
Combine complementary, orthogonal data sources rather than repeating correlated measurements when using serial testing to improve specificity.
Provide transparent reporting of the contextual features that drive a given AI alert to maintain clinical trust.
Establish clear allocation of legal liability among AI developers, platform operators, and clinicians for incorrect context-aware monitoring signals.
Establish clinical benefit of context-aware monitoring before assessing its cost-effectiveness.
Externally validate context-aware AI models in diverse populations before relying on their findings.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual/commentary paper discussing context-aware AI and Bayesian principles in screening rather than an empirical evaluation.
